name: Asteraceae
tip: What looks like one flower is a head of many tiny florets, often with strap-shaped rays round the edge and a ring of green bracts beneath. Dandelions, thistles, daisies, ragworts.

name: Rosaceae
tip: Usually 5 separate petals, many stamens and leafy stipules at the base of the leaf stalk; fruits often fleshy (hips, haws, brambles, cherries).

name: Poaceae
tip: Round, usually hollow stems with solid joints; long narrow leaves with a sheath wrapping the stem and a small flap (ligule) where blade meets sheath. Flowers in tiny green spikelets.

name: Fabaceae
tip: Pea-flowers: a large upper petal, two side wings and a boat-shaped keel. Leaves usually compound, often with tendrils; fruit a pod.

name: Cyperaceae
tip: Grass-like, but stems usually solid and triangular ('sedges have edges'); leaves in three ranks with no ligule flap. Cotton-grasses and spike-rushes belong here too.

name: Brassicaceae
tip: Four petals in a cross, six stamens (four long, two short); fruit a pod that splits from the bottom, leaving a papery central wall. Often a cress-like taste.

name: Caryophyllaceae
tip: Leaves in opposite pairs on stems swollen at the joints; five petals, often notched or deeply split (stitchworts, campions, chickweeds).

name: Apiaceae
tip: Tiny flowers in umbrella-shaped clusters (umbels), usually white; leaves often finely divided with a sheathing base; stems often hollow and ridged. Some are very poisonous.

name: Lamiaceae
tip: Square stems, opposite leaves, two-lipped flowers in rings up the stem; many smell when crushed (mints, dead-nettles, thymes).

name: Plantaginaceae
tip: A mixed family: plantains (ribbed leaves, brown flower spikes), speedwells (4 blue petals, 2 stamens), foxglove, toadflaxes, water-starworts.

name: Ranunculaceae
tip: Many stamens and separate petals or petal-like sepals; leaves often deeply lobed; fruit a cluster of small dry seeds. Buttercups, anemones, columbines, Clematis.

name: Orchidaceae
tip: Six petal-like parts, the lowest forming a distinctive lip, often patterned or spurred; leaves with parallel veins, sometimes spotted.

name: Polygonaceae
tip: A papery sheath (ochrea) round the stem above each leaf base; small flowers, 3 to 6 parts; fruit a 3-sided nut. Docks, sorrels, knotweeds, bistorts.

name: Amaranthaceae
tip: Small green flowers in dense clusters; leaves often mealy or fleshy; plants of bare and salty ground (goosefoots, oraches, glassworts).

name: Boraginaceae
tip: Rough, bristly hairs; flowers in coiled sprays that unroll as they open, often turning from pink to blue (forget-me-nots, comfreys, borage).

name: Amaryllidaceae
tip: Six-petalled flowers from a papery sheath; leaves strap-like from a bulb. Onions and garlics (umbels, onion smell), daffodils (with a trumpet), snowdrops.

name: Orobanchaceae
tip: Semi-parasites (eyebright, yellow-rattle, cow-wheat, lousewort) with two-lipped flowers; broomrapes have no green at all.

name: Ericaceae
tip: Small evergreen shrubs with bell- or urn-shaped flowers; leaves often tiny, needle-like or leathery (heathers, bilberry, rhododendron).

name: Juncaceae
tip: Grass-like; rushes have round stems, often filled with white pith; woodrushes have flat, hairy-edged leaves. Flowers small, brown, six-parted.

name: Iridaceae
tip: Sword-shaped leaves in a flat fan; showy flowers with 6 parts and 3 stamens (irises, crocuses, montbretia).

name: Asparagaceae
tip: Bulb or rhizome plants with parallel-veined leaves and six-parted flowers: bluebell, lily-of-the-valley, Solomon's-seal, butcher's-broom.

name: Geraniaceae
tip: Five separate petals and a long beak-like fruit (the 'crane's bill'); leaves usually lobed like a hand or finely divided.

name: Campanulaceae
tip: Bell-shaped, usually blue flowers; milky sap; ovary below the flower (harebell, bellflowers, sheep's-bit).

name: Primulaceae
tip: Five petals joined at the base, with the stamens opposite the petal lobes (primroses, cowslips, loosestrifes, scarlet pimpernel).

name: Crassulaceae
tip: Thick, fleshy, water-storing leaves; star-shaped flowers. Walls, rocks and dry places (stonecrops, houseleek, navelwort).

name: Caprifoliaceae
tip: Opposite leaves; includes honeysuckle, teasels and scabiouses (flower heads), valerians and snowberry.

name: Aspleniaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers; fronds uncurl from a crozier and carry spore patches underneath. Spleenworts, lady-fern, hard-fern, bladder-ferns.

name: Papaveraceae
tip: Poppies: 4 crumpled petals, many stamens, often milky or coloured sap. Fumitories and corydalis have small tubular, spurred flowers.

name: Saxifragaceae
tip: Small plants of rocks, mountains and damp places; five petals, often white; leaves frequently in a basal rosette. Golden-saxifrages have no petals.

name: Potamogetonaceae
tip: Water plants with floating or submerged leaves and small green flower spikes held above the water.

name: Onagraceae
tip: Four petals and a long, thin ovary below the flower; seeds often with silky hairs (willowherbs, evening-primroses, enchanter's-nightshade has 2 petals).

name: Salicaceae
tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins, male and female on separate plants; seeds with cottony hairs.

name: Rubiaceae
tip: Leaves in whorls (rings) of 4 to 12 round square stems; tiny 4-petalled flowers. Cleavers is the sticky one.

name: Polypodiaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers. Buckler-ferns, male-fern, shield-ferns and polypodies, with round spore patches on the frond underside.

name: Hypericaceae
tip: Opposite leaves, often with see-through dots when held up to the light; yellow flowers with many stamens in bundles.

name: Euphorbiaceae
tip: Spurges have milky sap and odd cup-like green flower clusters with no petals; dog's mercury has small green flowers on spikes.

name: Plumbaginaceae
tip: Coastal plants with leaves in a basal rosette; pink or lavender flowers with papery calyces (thrift heads, sea-lavender sprays).

name: Gentianaceae
tip: Hairless plants with opposite leaves and petals joined into a tube with 4 to 5 spreading lobes (centauries, gentians, yellow-wort).

name: Scrophulariaceae
tip: Figworts have square stems and small brown two-lipped flowers; mulleins have tall spikes of yellow flowers and often woolly leaves. Buddleja belongs here.

name: Araceae
tip: Lords-and-ladies: a hooded leaf-like spathe round a club-shaped spike, then red berries. Duckweeds (tiny floating green discs) are in this family too.

name: Oxalidaceae
tip: Clover-like leaves of three heart-shaped leaflets that fold down at night; five petals; sharp-tasting.

name: Solanaceae
tip: Five petals joined into a star or bell, with stamens forming a cone in the centre; fruit a berry or capsule. Many poisonous (bittersweet, deadly nightshade, henbane).

name: Violaceae
tip: Five unequal petals, the lowest with a backward spur; leaves often heart-shaped (violets and pansies).

name: Aizoaceae
tip: Introduced succulents with thick, three-sided or cylindrical leaves and large daisy-like flowers with many narrow petals; coastal cliffs.

name: Malvaceae
tip: Mallows: five notched petals and a central column of stamens; fruit like a round cheese. Limes are trees with a strap-like bract on the flower stalk.

name: Hydrocharitaceae
tip: Water plants: frogbit (floating, kidney-shaped leaves, 3 white petals), water-soldier, and the submerged waterweeds with whorled leaves.

name: Alismataceae
tip: Wetland plants with long-stalked basal leaves and flowers with 3 white or pale pink petals (water-plantains, arrowhead).

name: Araliaceae
tip: Ivy: evergreen climber with lobed leaves on climbing stems and ball-shaped umbels of greenish flowers in autumn. Marsh pennywort has round, umbrella-like leaves.

name: Lentibulariaceae
tip: Insect-catching plants: butterworts have sticky, pale green leaf rosettes; bladderworts float in water with tiny bladder traps.

name: Betulaceae
tip: Trees and shrubs with catkins in late winter or spring; fruits are nuts (hazel), tiny winged seeds (birch) or woody 'cones' (alder).

name: Pinaceae
tip: Conifers with needles (single, in pairs or in bunches) and woody cones (pines, spruces, firs, larch).

name: Liliaceae
tip: Bulb plants with large six-petalled flowers and parallel-veined leaves (fritillary, tulips, lilies, yellow star-of-Bethlehem).

name: Equisetaceae
tip: No flowers; jointed, ridged stems with rings of tiny teeth and whorls of thin green branches; spores in a cone at the stem tip.

name: Viburnaceae
tip: Shrubs with opposite leaves and flat-topped clusters of small white flowers, then berries (elder, guelder-rose, wayfaring-tree). Moschatel is a small herb.

name: Asphodelaceae
tip: Mostly introduced: New Zealand flax (huge leathery sword leaves), red-hot pokers, day-lilies; six-parted flowers.

name: Typhaceae
tip: Tall water-edge plants with long flat leaves: bulrushes have brown sausage-shaped heads; bur-reeds have spiky green balls.

name: Convolvulaceae
tip: Twining climbers with funnel-shaped flowers and arrow-shaped leaves. Dodders are leafless pink threads with no green.

name: Fagaceae
tip: Trees with catkins; fruit a nut in a cup or husk (acorns, beech-mast, sweet chestnuts).

name: Oleaceae
tip: Opposite leaves; flowers with 4 joined petals and 2 stamens, or no petals in ash. Ash has winged 'keys'; privet has black berries.

name: Sapindaceae
tip: Trees with opposite leaves: maples and sycamore have lobed leaves and paired winged fruits; horse-chestnut has hand-like compound leaves and conkers.

name: Urticaceae
tip: Small green flowers in dangling tassels; stinging nettle has stinging hairs, pellitory-of-the-wall does not.

name: Lycopodiaceae
tip: No flowers; creeping or upright stems densely covered in small, narrow, overlapping leaves; spores in cones or leaf bases.

name: Grossulariaceae
tip: Shrubs with lobed, maple-like leaves and hanging sprays of small flowers, then berries (currants, gooseberry, which is spiny).

name: Cistaceae
tip: Low, often woody-based plants of dry grassland with crumpled, short-lived yellow petals and many stamens.

name: Haloragaceae
tip: Submerged water plants with feathery leaves in whorls; small flowers on spikes above the water.

name: Linaceae
tip: Slender plants with narrow, untoothed leaves and 5 separate petals that drop quickly (fairy flax is white, flax blue).

name: Cornaceae
tip: Opposite leaves whose veins curve round towards the tip; 4-petalled flowers in flat clusters; dogwood has red winter stems.

name: Ulmaceae
tip: Trees with rough, toothed leaves that are lopsided at the base; fruit a flat papery wing round a seed.

name: Ophioglossaceae
tip: Small ferns with a single leaf and a separate spore-bearing spike or branch.

name: Cupressaceae
tip: Conifers with tiny scale-like or short prickly leaves; juniper has blue-black berry-like cones.

name: Aristolochiaceae
tip: Introduced woodland plants with heart- or kidney-shaped leaves and odd tubular or cup-shaped brownish flowers.

name: Montiaceae
tip: Small, fleshy, hairless plants with 5 white or pink petals; spring-beauty has a leaf collar round the stem below the flowers.

name: Resedaceae
tip: Spikes of small yellowish flowers with deeply cut petals and many stamens (weld, wild mignonette); bare chalky ground.

name: Pteridaceae
tip: Ferns: no flowers. Maidenhair fern has black stalks and fan-shaped leaflets; parsley fern grows in upland screes.

name: Nymphaeaceae
tip: Large round floating leaves with a slit to the centre; big white or yellow flowers floating or held just above the water.

name: Berberidaceae
tip: Spiny shrubs with yellow flowers and berries; Oregon-grape has holly-like compound leaves.

name: Vitaceae
tip: Woody climbers with tendrils; Virginia-creeper has hand-like leaves that turn red; small greenish flowers, then berries.

name: Polygalaceae
tip: Small plants of grassland and heath with blue, pink or white flowers: two large petal-like side sepals and a fringed lower petal.

name: Balsaminaceae
tip: Succulent stems; hooded, spurred flowers; seed pods that explode when touched (Himalayan balsam, touch-me-not).

name: Acanthaceae
tip: Introduced: large glossy, deeply lobed leaves and tall spikes of hooded flowers under spiny purple bracts.

name: Droseraceae
tip: Small bog plants with rosettes of round or narrow leaves covered in sticky red hairs that trap insects.

name: Isoetaceae
tip: No flowers; underwater rosettes of stiff, quill-like leaves at the bottom of clear lakes; spores at the leaf bases.

name: Lythraceae
tip: Purple-loosestrife: tall spikes of magenta flowers with 6 crinkled petals by water. Water-purslane is small and creeping.

name: Apocynaceae
tip: Trailing evergreen periwinkles with glossy opposite leaves and blue flowers whose 5 petals look twisted like a propeller.

name: Anacardiaceae
tip: Introduced stag's-horn sumach: shrub with velvety shoots, long pinnate leaves that turn red, dense red fruit clusters.

name: Phrymaceae
tip: Waterside plants with opposite leaves and large yellow, two-lipped, snapdragon-like flowers, often red-spotted.

name: Rutaceae
tip: Introduced aromatic shrubs with gland-dotted leaves (Mexican orange-blossom, rue).

name: Rhamnaceae
tip: Shrubs with small greenish 4 to 5-parted flowers and black berries; buckthorn is thorny with opposite leaves, alder buckthorn is thornless.

name: Hymenophyllaceae
tip: Tiny ferns with translucent fronds one cell thick, on wet shaded rocks and tree trunks in the west.

name: Celastraceae
tip: Spindle: shrub with green stems and pink four-lobed fruits with orange seeds. Grass-of-Parnassus: white 5-petalled flowers with fringed glands, wet places.

name: Juglandaceae
tip: Introduced trees with large aromatic pinnate leaves and catkins; walnuts, wing-nuts.

name: Acoraceae
tip: Iris-like leaves that smell of tangerines when crushed; a green finger-like flower spike sticking out sideways from a leaf-like stem.

name: Menyanthaceae
tip: Water plants: bogbean has three-part leaves and fringed white-pink flowers; fringed water-lily has small round floating leaves and yellow flowers.

name: Dennstaedtiaceae
tip: Fern: no flowers. Bracken has tall, single, much-divided fronds rising from underground stems, often in large stands.

name: Thymelaeaceae
tip: Shrubs with leathery leaves crowded towards the shoot tips and scented four-lobed flowers, then poisonous berries (mezereon, spurge-laurel).

name: Santalaceae
tip: Mistletoe: evergreen ball of forked green stems in trees, white berries. Bastard-toadflax: small parasitic herb of chalk grassland.

name: Zosteraceae
tip: Marine plants: long, grass-like ribbon leaves on sandy and muddy shores below the tide line.

name: Myricaceae
tip: Low shrub of bogs with grey-green leaves that smell resinous when crushed; catkins in spring.

name: Elatinaceae
tip: Tiny creeping plants of lake edges and mud with opposite leaves and minute pinkish flowers.

name: Ceratophyllaceae
tip: Rootless submerged water plants with whorls of stiff, forked, finely toothed leaves.

name: Cannabaceae
tip: Hop: twining rough-stemmed climber with lobed leaves and papery, cone-like female flower heads.

name: Juncaginaceae
tip: Grass-like plants of salt marsh and wet ground with fleshy, narrow leaves and a long slender spike of tiny green flowers.

name: Elaeagnaceae
tip: Spiny shrub with narrow silvery leaves and bright orange berries, mostly on sand dunes.

name: Selaginellaceae
tip: Small moss-like plant with tiny pointed leaves, in wet upland grassland and flushes; no flowers.

name: Pittosporaceae
tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs or trees with glossy leaves and small dark purple scented flowers; south-west coasts.

name: Ruppiaceae
tip: Submerged plants of brackish pools with thread-like leaves; flowers on long stalks.

name: Myrtaceae
tip: Introduced evergreen shrubs with aromatic, gland-dotted opposite leaves, white flowers with many stamens and edible berries.

name: Nothofagaceae
tip: Introduced trees planted for forestry, similar to beech but with smaller leaves.

name: Verbenaceae
tip: Wiry plant with square stems, lobed opposite leaves and long thin spikes of tiny lilac flowers.

name: Sarraceniaceae
tip: Introduced to a few bogs: leaves form upright tubes (pitchers) that trap insects.

name: Aquifoliaceae
tip: Evergreen tree or shrub with glossy, usually spiny leaves, small white 4-petalled flowers and red berries.

name: Alstroemeriaceae
tip: Garden escape with twisted leaf stalks and showy streaked flowers with 6 tepals.

name: Melanthiaceae
tip: Woodland plant with a single ring of four broad leaves and one starry green flower, then a black berry.

name: Marsileaceae
tip: Tiny fern of pond margins with grass-like leaves that uncurl like a crozier and pea-sized spore pills at the base.

name: Limnanthaceae
tip: Garden escape (poached-egg plant): white petals with yellow centres and divided leaves.

name: Lauraceae
tip: Bay: evergreen tree or shrub with aromatic leathery leaves used in cooking.

name: Frankeniaceae
tip: Low, mat-forming plant of salt marshes with tiny inrolled leaves and small pink flowers.

name: Eriocaulaceae
tip: Western Scottish and Irish lakes: underwater rosettes of grass-like leaves and small white button-heads on leafless stalks above the water.

name: Gunneraceae
tip: Introduced: gigantic rhubarb-like leaves on prickly stalks, with a huge cone-like spike of tiny flowers.

name: Butomaceae
tip: Tall water-edge plant with three-angled leaves and an umbel of pink six-petalled flowers.

name: Cabombaceae
tip: Introduced aquarium plant: submerged fan-shaped, finely divided opposite leaves and small white flowers.

name: Buxaceae
tip: Evergreen shrub with small, glossy, oval opposite leaves and tiny greenish flowers; chalk slopes and gardens.

name: Calceolariaceae
tip: Introduced: pouched, slipper-shaped yellow two-lipped flowers.

name: Colchicaceae
tip: Pink crocus-like flowers in autumn without leaves; broad leaves appear in spring. Poisonous.

name: Cucurbitaceae
tip: Climber with coiled tendrils, rough lobed leaves, greenish-white flowers and red berries.

name: Diapensiaceae
tip: Very rare: cushion plant on one Scottish mountain, with white five-petalled flowers.

name: Dioscoreaceae
tip: Twining climber with glossy heart-shaped leaves, small greenish flowers and red berries; no tendrils.

name: Pontederiaceae
tip: Introduced water plants with glossy leaves and spikes of blue flowers.

name: Portulacaceae
tip: Fleshy, sprawling annual with small yellow flowers; a garden weed.

name: Polemoniaceae
tip: Ladder-like pinnate leaves and clusters of blue bell-shaped flowers; limestone in northern England.

name: Paulowniaceae
tip: Introduced tree with very large, soft, opposite leaves and upright clusters of violet foxglove-like flowers.

name: Phytolaccaceae
tip: Introduced tall plant with reddish stems, upright spikes of small flowers and dark purple berries.

name: Moraceae
tip: Introduced tree with heart-shaped, sometimes lobed leaves, milky sap and blackberry-like fruits.

name: Osmundaceae
tip: Large fern of wet places whose fertile fronds end in rusty-brown, flower-like spore clusters; no true flowers.

name: Paeoniaceae
tip: Garden escape with large red flowers and divided leaves.

name: Nartheciaceae
tip: Bog plant with flat, sword-shaped leaves and spikes of starry orange-yellow flowers.

name: Scheuchzeriaceae
tip: Very rare bog plant with grass-like leaves that have a pore at the tip, and a few yellowish-green flowers.

name: Salviniaceae
tip: Introduced tiny floating fern forming red or green carpets on still water; no flowers.

name: Saururaceae
tip: Introduced: heart-shaped leaves smelling of orange peel and spikes of tiny flowers with four white petal-like bracts.

name: Tropaeolaceae
tip: Garden escape with round, umbrella-like leaves and orange or yellow spurred flowers.

name: Tofieldiaceae
tip: Small northern plant of wet flushes with a fan of short flat leaves and a tight head of pale greenish-white flowers.

name: Simaroubaceae
tip: Introduced tree with very long pinnate leaves, unpleasant-smelling when crushed, and twisted winged fruits.

name: Cyatheaceae
tip: Introduced tree-fern (Dicksonia) with a fibrous trunk topped by large fronds; south-west gardens and woods.

name: Taxaceae
tip: Evergreen conifer with flat, dark green needles in two rows and red fleshy cups around single seeds; no cones. All parts except the red flesh are poisonous.

name: Lamium album
tip: Looks like a stinging nettle but has white flowers and does not sting.

name: Lamium purpureum
tip: Upper leaves crowded and tinged purple; an annual of gardens and bare ground.

name: Lamium amplexicaule
tip: Upper leaves have no stalk and clasp the stem in pairs beneath the flowers.

name: Lamium galeobdolon
tip: Yellow flowers with reddish streaks on the lower lip; an ancient-woodland indicator.

name: Glechoma hederacea
tip: Kidney-shaped, round-toothed leaves on long creeping stems; smells pungent when crushed.

name: Prunella vulgaris
tip: Dense, squarish flower head with purple-tinged bracts and a pair of leaves just below it. Common in lawns.

name: Stachys sylvatica
tip: Dark wine-red flowers with white markings; stinks when crushed.

name: Stachys palustris
tip: Paler pinkish-purple flowers than Hedge Woundwort; narrow leaves with little or no stalk.

name: Mentha aquatica
tip: Rounded lilac flower head at the stem tip; strong mint smell.

name: Mentha arvensis
tip: Flowers only in whorls up the stem; the stem ends in leaves, not flowers.

name: Thymus drucei
tip: Low mats of tiny leaves; stems hairy on two opposite sides only.

name: Origanum vulgare
tip: Loose, branched clusters with purple bracts; smells of oregano.

name: Teucrium scorodonia
tip: Pale greenish-yellow flowers with no upper lip; wrinkled, sage-like leaves; acid soils.

name: Ajuga reptans
tip: Glossy leaves, leafy runners and a very short upper lip.

name: Galeopsis tetrahit
tip: Bristly stem that swells just below each pair of leaves.

name: Ballota nigra
tip: Rank-smelling hedgerow plant; the calyx has broad, spreading teeth.

name: Clinopodium vulgare
tip: Flower whorls wrapped in long, bristly hairs, so they look woolly; only faintly aromatic.

name: Lycopus europaeus
tip: Deeply toothed to lobed leaves; tiny purple-dotted white flowers in tight whorls.

name: Scutellaria galericulata
tip: Flowers in pairs in the leaf axils, all facing one way; calyx has a small hump.

name: Betonica officinalis
tip: Rosette of long-stalked, oblong leaves; reddish-purple flowers in a dense spike.

name: Ranunculus repens
tip: Long runners that root at the joints; leaves with three leaflets, the middle one on its own stalk; flower stalks furrowed.

name: Ranunculus acris
tip: Tall and hairy with no runners; leaves deeply cut like a hand; flower stalks round and smooth, not furrowed.

name: Ficaria verna
tip: Early spring; glossy heart-shaped leaves; 8 to 12 narrow, shiny yellow petals; often small bulbils where the leaves join the stem.

name: Caltha palustris
tip: Large glossy kidney-shaped leaves; big golden cup flowers with no green sepals beneath; marshes and wet woods.

name: Ranunculus flammula
tip: Narrow, spear-shaped leaves and small yellow buttercup flowers; wet ground and pond edges.

name: Anemone nemorosa
tip: Spring carpets in old woods; a single white flower, often pink-tinged beneath, above a ring of three divided leaves.

name: Ranunculus bulbosus
tip: Sepals folded right back down the flower stalk; stem base swollen like a small bulb; dry grassland.

name: Aquilegia vulgaris
tip: Nodding flowers with five hooked spurs, usually violet-blue; leaves divided into rounded, lobed leaflets.

name: Ranunculus sceleratus
tip: Hairless, shiny, often hollow stem; tiny pale yellow flowers with a large green fruiting head in the middle; muddy pond edges.

name: Ranunculus hederaceus
tip: Small creeping plant of shallow water and mud with only ivy-shaped leaves (no thread-like ones) and tiny white flowers.

name: Clematis vitalba
tip: Woody climber over hedges and scrub on chalk and limestone; creamy flowers with 4 sepals; feathery 'old man's beard' seed heads.

name: Ranunculus auricomus
tip: Woodland buttercup whose petals are often missing or misshapen; rounded basal leaves, narrow finger-like stem leaves.

name: Helleborus foetidus
tip: Evergreen; dark leaves cut into narrow fingers; nodding pale green bells rimmed with purple in late winter.

name: Ranunculus lingua
tip: Tall water-edge plant with long narrow leaves and large (3 to 5 cm) yellow flowers.

name: Ranunculus aquatilis
tip: White flowers on the water; both floating lobed leaves and submerged thread-like leaves; ponds and ditches. Water-crowfoots are a tricky group: check with a specialist.

name: Thalictrum minus
tip: Finely divided leaves like maidenhair fern; loose sprays of small drooping greenish-yellow flowers that are mostly stamens. Dunes and limestone.

name: Ranunculus omiophyllus
tip: Like Ivy-leaved Crowfoot but leaves more deeply lobed and flowers larger; western, on acid mud and in streams.

name: Ranunculus trichophyllus
tip: Only short, submerged thread-like leaves that collapse out of water; small white flowers; ponds and ditches.

name: Trollius europaeus
tip: Large globe-shaped yellow flowers of incurved petals; damp upland meadows and streamsides in the north.

name: Ranunculus peltatus
tip: Floating rounded leaves plus thread-like submerged ones; large white flowers; ponds and slow water.

name: Ranunculus penicillatus
tip: Long trailing submerged threads in flowing rivers, sometimes with floating leaves; large white flowers.

name: Aconitum napellus
tip: Tall spikes of deep blue-violet hooded flowers; deeply cut hand-shaped leaves; shady streamsides. Very poisonous.

name: Thalictrum flavum
tip: Tall plant of fens and riversides with dense clusters of fluffy pale yellow stamens; leaves with many leaflets.

name: Ranunculus sardous
tip: Like Bulbous Buttercup (sepals bent back) but paler yellow, hairier and with no swollen stem base; damp ground, often near the coast.

name: Thalictrum alpinum
tip: Small mountain plant with a few drooping purplish flowers on a slender stalk; leaves with small rounded leaflets.

name: Ranunculus parviflorus
tip: Sprawling hairy annual with tiny yellow flowers and rounded, lobed leaves; seeds covered in hooked bumps.

name: Helleborus viridis
tip: Dies down in winter; flat, open green flowers in early spring; leaves cut into toothed fingers; woods on lime.

name: Ranunculus fluitans
tip: Very long, dark green, tassel-like submerged leaves in fast rivers; no floating leaves.

name: Ranunculus circinatus
tip: Stiff, flat, circular fans of short thread-like leaves that keep their shape when lifted out of water.

name: Ranunculus baudotii
tip: Water-crowfoot of brackish coastal ditches and pools; floating and thread-like leaves.

name: Myosurus minimus
tip: Tiny plant with grass-like leaves; the fruiting head stretches into a long, thin, mouse-tail spike.

name: Ranunculus arvensis
tip: Rare cornfield weed with pale yellow flowers and large seeds covered in sharp spines.

name: Ranunculus tripartitus
tip: Rare, south-west; tiny white flowers; deeply three-lobed floating leaves, sometimes thread-like ones too; seasonal pools.

name: Adonis annua
tip: Rare cornfield annual with feathery leaves and blood-red flowers with a dark centre.

name: Pulsatilla vulgaris
tip: Silky-hairy plant of chalk and limestone grassland with large purple bell flowers in spring, then feathery seed heads.

name: Actaea spicata
tip: Rare, in limestone woods and pavement in northern England; fluffy spikes of small white flowers, then black berries.

name: Ranunculus reptans
tip: Very rare; slender arching runners that root at each joint, with narrow leaves; stony lake shores.

name: Ranunculus ophioglossifolius
tip: Very rare; oval to heart-shaped lower leaves and small pale yellow flowers in muddy pools.

name: Eranthis hyemalis
tip: Garden escape in woods and parks; yellow cup flowers in mid-winter sitting on a ruff of deeply cut leaves.

name: Anemone blanda
tip: Garden escape; low plant with many narrow blue, pink or white petals in early spring.

name: Anemone apennina
tip: Garden escape like Wood Anemone but with sky-blue flowers of 10 to 15 narrow petals.

name: Helleborus argutifolius
tip: Garden escape with leathery evergreen leaves of three spiny-toothed leaflets and pale green cup flowers in winter.

name: Helleborus orientalis
tip: Garden escape; nodding cup flowers in late winter and spring, cream, pink or purple; leathery leaves.

name: Nigella damascena
tip: Garden escape; blue flowers in a ruff of thread-like bracts; swollen, balloon-like seed pods.

name: Consolida ajacis
tip: Garden escape; spikes of blue, pink or white flowers with one long spur; very finely divided leaves.
